evals.prompt: Create a new baseapp-backend package called 'bookmarks' that lets any object be bookmarked by a profile. Scaffold it.
assertions: Creates the package under baseapp/bookmarks/, not baseapp_bookmarks/ at the repo root
Creates both apps.py (PackageConfig) and plugin.py (BookmarksPlugin)
Sets AppConfig.name to the dotted path 'baseapp.bookmarks' and label to the underscore form 'baseapp_bookmarks'
Adds the entry point to [project.entry-points."baseapp.plugins"] in pyproject.toml, not to a setup.cfg
Does NOT create a migrations/ directory for the swappable model

evals.prompt: My new block baseapp/bookmarks is in INSTALLED_APPS but plugin_registry.get('INSTALLED_APPS') doesn't show anything from it and its GraphQL queries are missing. Why?
assertions: Identifies that plugin.package_name must be the dotted import path 'baseapp.bookmarks' since it is matched against INSTALLED_APPS
Distinguishes package_name from name (the underscore identity form)
Mentions that the app must be added before plugin_registry.load_from_installed_apps(...) is called
Mentions that the distribution must be reinstalled for an entry-point change to take effect
Does not suggest editing setup.cfg

evals.prompt: Our Message resolver reads root.deleted and root.message_type, but neither is exposed in GraphQL. The messages list issues one extra query per message. Fix it.
assertions: Adds the fields to optimizer.only_fields inside pre_optimization_hook
Explains that the optimizer defers columns not selected by GraphQL, so each access triggers a per-row refresh_from_db
Calls super().pre_optimization_hook(queryset, optimizer)
Does not suggest graphene_django_optimizer or gql_optimizer.query()
Recommends pinning the result with a query-count test

evals.prompt: I'm adding a bookmarksCount field to a shared GraphQL interface that Comment, Page and ContentPost all mix in. How do I keep it from doing a query per row without every consuming block changing its own code?
assertions: Recommends attaching a function to the field's optimizer_hook attribute rather than editing each consumer's pre_optimization_hook
Explains the hook fires only when the field is selected
Builds the subquery from compiler.optimizer.model rather than a hardcoded model
Guards against compiler.optimizer or its model being None
Mentions the interface needs Meta.model so the AST walker descends into the inline fragment

evals.prompt: I added a pre_optimization_hook to ProfileObjectType but the profiles list query count didn't change at all. What's going on?
assertions: Identifies that graphene_django.filter.DjangoFilterConnectionField does not run the query_optimizer compiler
Recommends switching to query_optimizer.DjangoConnectionField
Notes that filtering still works via Meta.filterset_class on the optimized class
Warns that neighbouring code is an unreliable guide because the repo is mid-migration
Suggests capturing the query count before and after the switch

evals.prompt: Add a bookmarks_count to profiles that clients can also sort by, without a query per profile.
assertions: Stores the counter in a DocumentId-keyed sidecar metadata model rather than a column on Profile
Adds an annotate_queryset classmethod using a correlated Subquery with OuterRef('pk')
Wraps the annotation in Coalesce with a default so targets without a metadata row cost nothing
Exposes a public (non-underscore) annotation name so OrderingFilter can sort on it
Gives the service getter a hasattr fallback so correctness does not depend on the annotation

evals.prompt: My block should show a profile field when baseapp_profiles is installed and work fine when it isn't. How do I wire that up?
assertions: Guards the model field with apps.is_installed and mixes it in at class-definition time
Uses apply_if_installed for the GraphQL Meta.fields entry
Declares baseapp_profiles in optional_packages, not required_packages
Guards any shared_services.get(...) result against None
Adds a test under tests/integration/ using with_disabled_apps_context

evals.prompt: Add a new ObjectType for the Bookmark model. The neighbouring blocks mix in gql_optimizer.OptimizedDjangoObjectType — should I?
assertions: Says no, and subclasses only baseapp_core.graphql.DjangoObjectType
Explains that gql_optimizer.query() is never called so the mixin is inert
Identifies graphene-django-query-optimizer (query_optimizer) as the live library
Notes baseapp_core.DjangoObjectType already subclasses query_optimizer.DjangoObjectType
Does not recommend gql_optimizer.resolver_hints or gql_optimizer.query
